scope: Specification conflicts and per-feature verification tasks; these are not missing-method guesses.

gaps.title: Bucket PUT defaults, ACL omission, immutable inputs and revision/error semantics need provider evidence
gaps.observed_evidence: The update reference warns that omitted metadata may change; the overview contrasts PATCH with full replacement rather than directly describing PUT. The pinned v2 UpdateBucketRequest mask * equates it with JSON update; proto SHA-256 a0df6132967b97a89be248f1f24d277ee8df8f8d885db1d4af6249469ff0c1cf. Discovery revision 20261013 SHA-256 1f74b7a93b3d2872cc332fc20dafae1657fc255930ce336618bea3d0b4d95ae0 does not establish omitted JSON defaults or null scalars. Both the method page and Discovery annotations.required [storage.buckets.update] mark acl[] required; the method says an empty list is ignored. Accepting omitted acl for SDK full-resource round trips without changing permissions is a local choice. Local replacement clears omitted/null labels, reuses the creation-only STANDARD default for omitted class and resets omitted settings to false; null label values/class are invalid, native null booleans invalid, legacy null booleans false, following insert/PATCH local choices. Insert-only/immutable/reserved fields absent from update's writable list inherit PATCH's fail-closed 501 or unchanged-location/name-ignore local rules. IAM policy etag preservation is also local. Every success advances revision once, including no-effect replacement; HTTP invalid bodies, including 65 labels, precede missing lookup and stale conditions (400), while unsupported fields return 501 before conditions. Transactional authorization precedes conditions, which precede catalog validation (direct invalid-label calls with stale conditions return 412). Contract and executable acceptance cases: docs/en/slices/bucket-metadata-put.md.
gaps.required_resolution: Keep complete method PARTIAL. Obtain authoritative clarification or explicitly authorized provider evidence for omitted-field defaults and null scalars/maps. Determine independently whether omitted acl returns 400 required, versus accepting acl:[]; local acceptance does not resolve the mandatory annotation. Determine whether storage.buckets.getIpFilter is required for the modeled response without ipFilter and whether ignored acl:[] requires storage.buckets.setIamPolicy. Determine responses for identical, changed and null insert-only/immutable/reserved inputs: location, customPlacementConfig, hierarchicalNamespace, objectRetention, satisfiesPZI/PZS and body name differing from the path. Resolve no-effect revisions, HTTP adapter versus catalog and combined/missing-bucket error precedence, unknown/output-only inputs, etag/timestamp (including whether bucket metadata updates change IAM policy etag) and propagation behavior. SPEC-017 separately owns strict authentication and full-projection permission questions. Do not infer PUT semantics from PATCH or reference behavior; the pinned reference has no bucket PUT route and observed PUT returns 404. SDK/local tests do not establish provider parity. Preserve declared native-to-legacy metageneration-1 rendering limitations.

gaps.title: Bucket PATCH legacy input, deletion, revision and propagation semantics remain partly unverified
gaps.observed_evidence: Official partial updates and label examples establish merge and key-null removal. Whole-map null clearing interprets the general deletion rule; direct legacy JSON behavior for storageClass null/defaults, native null boolean rejection, unknown/output-only input and no-effect revision increment is not established. Local PATCH validates permissive bodies before missing lookup, increments every successful request once, and uses millisecond clock time without artificial advancement. The pinned reference ignores labels/class/conditions, resets omitted booleans and keeps fixed revision fields; both local profiles deliberately preserve omitted settings and expose mutable state after PATCH. Same-profile resource round trips and unchanged case-insensitive location are supported; a native-created metageneration-1 bucket reopened in legacy can hide class/labels, and native insert location comparison remains case-sensitive. Contract: docs/en/slices/bucket-metadata-patch.md; comparison: docs/en/evidence/bucket-metadata-patch-comparison.md.
gaps.required_resolution: Keep whole method PARTIAL with unsupported ACL/billing/full-projection and advanced-field cases. Obtain authoritative clarification or explicitly authorized service evidence for scalar/map deletion defaults, legacy unknown/output-only inputs, no-effect revision, missing-bucket/combined error order, etag/timestamp and configuration propagation; SPEC-017 separately owns strict authentication wire questions. Do not infer service parity from ignored reference inputs or local SDK success. Resolve carry-over rendering and insert location differences in their owning slices. No real-cloud test is authorized by this evidence.

gaps.title: Generation-specific deletion condition selection needs authoritative clarification
gaps.observed_evidence: The delete reference selects a revision with generation but describes conditions using current/live generation wording; the preconditions guide describes the targeted resource and explicitly selected noncurrent versions. Local deletion evaluates all four conditions against the selected revision and its metageneration, including not-match when no live version remains. versioned_delete_and_permanent_generation_delete verifies this local choice; docs/en/slices/bucket-versioning-holds.md records the source distinction. No provider differential request was made.
gaps.required_resolution: Obtain authoritative clarification or explicitly authorized provider evidence for selected noncurrent revisions with another live revision or no live revision, all four conditions and combined failures. Preserve atomic selected-generation conditions and keep complete provider parity pending.

gaps.title: Event hold omission, null, propagation and error wire details remain unverified
gaps.observed_evidence: HTTP tests verify inherited holds on media/multipart/resumable publication, explicit false overrides, rejected protected mutations and selected-generation release. Local PUT omission preserves a hold, null is invalid, false is omitted from object resources, configuration effects are immediate and exact provider error messages/combined failure precedence are unverified. The pinned Go high-level bucket Create serializer omits DefaultEventBasedHold; SDK coverage creates that setting using official JSON Buckets.Insert then uses high-level Writer/Attrs/Update/Delete.
gaps.required_resolution: Reconcile null/omitted PUT handling, false representation, propagation and exact error precedence through authoritative clarification or authorized provider observations. Implement bucket metadata updates as separate slices; temporary holds and retention interactions remain explicit pending work.

gaps.title: Discovery resumable protocol path differs from the documented and Go SDK initiation path
gaps.observed_evidence: Discovery revision 20261013 declares /resumable/upload/storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o as the resumable protocol path. The performing guide and API v0.307.0 generated ObjectsInsertCall instead initiate POST /upload/storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o?uploadType=resumable. The slice requires the latter verified source path and does not infer whether the former is an accepted alias. The pinned gensupport transport then uses POST to the returned session URI, unlike the guide's PUT, and requires HTTP 200 plus X-HTTP-Status-Code-Override: 308 when X-GUploader-No-308: yes is sent; both request forms are explicitly included in the contract.
gaps.required_resolution: Retain the guide/SDK initiation path and PUT plus pinned SDK POST coverage. Obtain authoritative clarification or explicitly authorized differential evidence for the Discovery alias before claiming the entire objects.insert upload protocol surface. Do not treat an untested alias as GA or remove the SDK's no-308 header. Fetched digests are in docs/en/sources.md; scope and cases are in docs/en/slices/resumable-upload.md.

gaps.title: Resumable error, total, checksum and terminal-session edge parity needs independent evidence
gaps.observed_evidence: Sources establish seven-day lifetime, persisted-prefix immutability, 308/Range with no Range for zero persisted bytes, unknown totals, final 200/201 and JSON cancellation 499. The concept page gives 410 for an invalid URI before one week and 404 after one week; the performing guide promises only a future 4xx after cancellation. They do not establish exact deadline equality, cancellation-repeat/completed-DELETE body shape, failed-session retention, zero-body bytes */N finalization distinction, total/header conflict errors, offset-gap or concurrent-writer errors, chunk alignment enforcement, final custom-metadata key conflicts, or MIME precedence when metadata conflicts with X-Upload-Content-Type. Local choices are 604800 seconds with expiry at equality, cancelled-session 410 before deadline and 404 at/after, completed-session DELETE 410 before expiry, and committed cancellation 499 even if physical cleanup fails, with visible journaled cleanup retried by maintenance. Other local choices are bounded completed-resource retention, 400 malformed/gap/total errors, 503 concurrent-writer/admission rejection, complete-request offset checkpoints, and metadata contentType before X-Upload-Content-Type. Pinned Go sends an empty final POST with bytes */offset for an exact chunk multiple and whole-object CRC32C in final X-Goog-Hash. The general concept page recommends Content-MD5, whereas JSON-specific validation documents final X-Goog-Hash; Content-MD5 stays explicitly unsupported in the existing local JSON profile. Checked official JSON sources do not define fake-gcs-server's alternate x-goog-upload-* command protocol. No real-service differential test was run.
gaps.required_resolution: Keep the exact supported subset and explicit local choices in docs/en/slices/resumable-upload.md; never claim provider error/edge parity from local tests. Local committed terminal validation failures preserve their original error response when physical cleanup fails; diagnostics and the deletion journal retain the cleanup failure for maintenance retry, and successful cleanup is not repeated before expiry. Obtain authoritative clarification or explicitly authorized cloud evidence for error bodies/order, invalid-session lifetime boundaries, completed/failed session retention, status versus empty finalization, length/total conflicts, concurrent/invalid chunks, metadata/header precedence, Content-MD5 and alternate upload command applicability. Keep x-goog-upload command variants outside the verified slice and reject recognized unsupported semantics. Completed-session protocol state is separate from SPEC-013 token-keyed response replay.

gaps.title: Resumable bearer capability and changed-permission/precondition evaluation timing need reconciliation
gaps.observed_evidence: The performing/concept guides say anyone holding the session URI may upload without further authentication. The performing guide also warns that changed bucket permissions can cause a nonretryable 4xx. Objects.insert requires create plus delete for overwrite and says initiation query parameters are ignored in subsequent PUT requests, without specifying all advisory-versus-final checks or the principal used after delegation. The slice preserves the initiating authorization context, permits delegated chunk/status/cancel without reauthentication, and re-evaluates that context and all four stored generation/metageneration conditions atomically at final publication. Bucket incarnation prevents deletion/recreation from reusing stale authority. The existing 412-before-overwrite-403 local order remains SPEC-017; no provider timing/order is inferred.
gaps.required_resolution: Verify permission revocation, creator-only concurrent overwrite, deleted/recreated buckets, delegated requests with different/missing credentials, and all four precondition races locally without weakening atomic publication. Obtain authoritative clarification or explicitly authorized service observations of the checked principal, permission recheck timing and condition/permission error ordering before claiming exact provider parity. Do not require a fresh bearer header for possession-authorized session requests or mistake invocation tokens for capability authorization.

gaps.title: Fixed advertised resumable Location does not implement automatic allowed-origin selection
gaps.observed_evidence: src/config.rs exposes only fixed api_base_url; src/url.rs normalizes absolute HTTP(S) bases and optional proxy prefixes. The design/onboarding proposal describes validated_request_origin with allowed authorities, but that mode, allowlist and trusted-proxy configuration do not exist. The slice chooses the actual fixed advertised endpoint and never trusts Host/Forwarded/X-Forwarded-*; host, peer and browser-address cases use explicitly reachable configurations. One fixed origin does not automatically address disjoint host and Compose DNS spaces. Browser CORS enforcement is outside this slice.
gaps.required_resolution: Verify host SDK, Compose-peer and browser-address reachability with their advertised configurations and hostile header tests. Preserve the fixed-base security boundary and document a common reachable DNS/proxy endpoint or separate configurations. Implement and verify an explicit allowlist/trust model before offering automatic request-origin Location selection; do not claim the broader automatic multi-origin proposal complete from fixed-origin tests.

gaps.title: Shared-listener XML names colliding with JSON namespaces need routing evidence
gaps.observed_evidence: The endpoint reference defines JSON and XML /bucket/object paths on storage.googleapis.com without resolving every collision. Local reserved paths are exactly /storage/v1, /upload/storage/v1, /download/storage/v1, /batch/storage/v1 and /_internal, including slash-delimited descendants. Other objects in buckets storage, upload, download and batch remain reachable. Unknown reserved paths do not fall through to XML; url public rejects colliding final bucket/object paths. This is a shared-listener restriction, not evidence that Google reserves these names. DESIGN-047 establishes exact decoding within this declared routing profile, not provider collision parity.
gaps.required_resolution: Record the exact reserved local prefixes and maintain positive/negative precedence tests. Obtain authoritative clarification or explicitly authorized service routing observations for colliding bucket/object names and encoded aliases before widening path-style compatibility; never reroute an existing JSON operation or helper/admin path as an XML object.

gaps.title: Invalid bucket segments retain JSON unknown-route errors
gaps.observed_evidence: The XML adapter selects only a valid raw bucket segment. Invalid or percent-encoded bucket segments retain the JSON-style 404 unknown-route response; valid bucket/object paths use XML errors. tests/auth_http/xml.rs asserts this boundary, including HEAD body suppression. The checked references do not establish this shared-listener error-format choice.
gaps.required_resolution: Keep complete XML method parity PARTIAL. Obtain authoritative routing/error-format clarification or explicitly authorized differential observations for invalid and encoded bucket segments before claiming provider parity. Preserve the negative unknown-route tests. See SPEC-XML-PREFIX and docs/en/slices/public-object-reads.md.

gaps.title: XML unknown input and metadata representation rejection remain local choices
gaps.observed_evidence: Unknown XML query keys and unsupported x-goog inputs return 501 NotImplemented; malformed query encoding, duplicate selectors and malformed numeric conditions return 400. x-goog-api-client and a single nonempty x-goog-gcs-idempotency-token are accepted as read telemetry without response replay; empty/repeated tokens return 400. JSON custom metadata that cannot be represented in HTTP or collides after case folding makes XML reads return 501 without changing stored metadata. Local XML ETags are quoted hexadecimal MD5; private default Cache-Control is private, max-age=0. Public defaults are public, max-age=3600, while nonpublic JSON remains no-cache. These local checks do not establish exhaustive Google error/header parity.
gaps.required_resolution: Retain complete XML method PARTIAL status and explicit rejection. Reconcile unknown-input and custom-metadata behavior with authorized provider evidence; SPEC-012 owns ETag/header/custom encoding parity, SPEC-015 owns JSON metadata/cache input parity, SPEC-017 owns authentication errors and SPEC-XML-PREFIX owns namespace routing. Accepted read retry telemetry must not be claimed as token-keyed response replay.

gaps.title: JSON range fallback and empty-object response parity need direct evidence
gaps.observed_evidence: Malformed/non-bytes/multiple/repeated ranges and nonzero empty-object suffixes locally fall back to complete 200 responses under RFC 9110. Google documents single ranges and 416 reason, but not every fallback, exact 416 message or exhaustive error header. The XML public-read contract reuses these fallback rules without claiming XML parity. The method-specific HEAD reference says Range adds Content-Range but otherwise has no effect; the general Range reference describes 206 without spelling out a HEAD exception. Local HEAD uses 200/full Content-Length and an empty body, adding bytes start-end/size for a satisfiable range and bytes */size for an unsatisfiable range. Exact unsatisfiable HEAD status/header parity remains an open question; the wire test records local behavior only.
gaps.required_resolution: Obtain authoritative clarification or explicitly authorized differential evidence before claiming exact Google fallback, empty-suffix and error-header parity. Preserve the local rules in docs/en/slices/json-object-range.md. Include XML fallback/empty-object cases and HEAD satisfiable/unsatisfiable ranges in opted-in evidence; retain the specific HEAD rule and document any departure instead of treating GET and HEAD as identical.

gaps.title: JSON If-Range validator support needs an established Google contract
gaps.observed_evidence: The checked Google JSON references do not establish the If-Range ETag/date subset; RFC definitions alone do not prove provider support. Both forms return explicit local 501.
gaps.required_resolution: Establish Google's JSON If-Range contract before implementing validators; retain explicit rejection and method PARTIAL status.

gaps.title: Object listing zero-size and cursor edge semantics require direct evidence
gaps.observed_evidence: Discovery revision 20261013 defines uint32 maxResults minimum 0, default 1000 and a 1000 cap, while JSON references do not settle zero-page progress. The implementation treats zero as default, matching existing bucket listing. Trailing marker item/prefix representations count separately for size-one pages. Tokens bind bucket, prefix, delimiter, offsets, trailing-delimiter flag and projection through the existing corruption checksum; page size may change. These tokens are not cryptographically authenticated snapshots or Google-compatible encodings.
gaps.required_resolution: Keep whole method/pagination claims PARTIAL and document the local rules. Obtain authorized differential evidence for zero, marker accounting and token-query changes before claiming exact edge compatibility; retain bounded seek and mutation-between-pages tests. See docs/en/slices/json-object-list.md and docs/en/evidence/object-list.md.

gaps.title: Empty object-list fields and slash-specific delimiter wording need reconciliation
gaps.observed_evidence: The method page includes slash-specific common-prefix wording, but Discovery and the response field description explicitly preserve the requested delimiter. The implementation follows the latter for arbitrary complete delimiters. Empty items/prefixes/nextPageToken are omitted, consistent with the pinned official Go Objects response omitempty schema; the method reference does not explicitly establish service wire omission. No real-cloud request was made.
gaps.required_resolution: Preserve multi-character/multibyte delimiter and empty-response wire tests, document the source distinction, and obtain authorized direct service evidence before claiming complete response-shape parity. Full projection still omits unsupported ACL/owner fields and production permissions remain unimplemented.

gaps.required_resolution: The overview states HNS-only; omission of that restriction on the dedicated page does not prove its removal. Reconcile current compatibility tables, release notes and an authorized real-service fixture before choosing a strict rule. Never substitute copy plus delete for atomic move.
gaps.observed_evidence: The objects resource overview describes move as HNS-only. The dedicated move page, updated 2026-10-20, describes same-bucket atomic moves without restating that restriction. Omission of a restriction is not evidence that it was removed.

gaps.required_resolution: A registered Operations service does not guarantee all five methods for every operation. Verify unsupported/cancellation behavior; Delete is not Cancel and Wait is not an unconditional completion promise.

gaps.title: Object not-match status and combined-condition error precedence need reconciliation
gaps.required_resolution: Keep a false GET not-match distinguishable from match failure so reads can return an empty 304. Determine mutation not-match status and precedence for missing objects, exact generation selection and multiple failing conditions from authoritative clarification or explicitly authorized differential tests. Until then document any local mutation/precedence rule as a deviation; never mutate on a failed condition.
gaps.observed_evidence: The preconditions guide assigns 304 to ifGenerationNotMatch and ifMetagenerationNotMatch without a method restriction; the JSON error catalog describes failed preconditions under 412 conditionNotMet and conditional false requests under 304 notModified. Method pages describe comparisons but do not establish combined-condition/missing-resource error precedence. Discovery revision 20261013 supplies int64 parameters, not evaluation order. See docs/en/slices/json-object-media.md.

gaps.title: Ordinary JSON media GET redirect is not described consistently across references
gaps.required_resolution: Reconcile the 303 mediaDownloadRedirect rule with the ordinary get endpoint description. Implement a documented redirect or explicitly declare direct 200 a local deviation. Preserve encoded names, conditions and the externally configured endpoint in any Location. Do not invent mediaDownload.path in Discovery.
gaps.observed_evidence: The error catalog says alt=media without the /download prefix issues 303 with Location. The objects.get page says alt=media retrieves data at /storage/v1 without describing a redirect. Request endpoints calls /download/storage/v1 optional. gaps.title: JSON media checksum edge cases and Content-MD5 acceptance are unspecified
gaps.required_resolution: Support the explicitly documented JSON media X-Goog-Hash mechanism. Verify JSON Content-MD5 acceptance, repeated/conflicting algorithm values, unknown algorithm handling and exact malformed/mismatch error reasons before claiming parity. Reject unimplemented checksum inputs explicitly and record parser/reason choices as local; do not infer JSON Content-MD5 from the XML API.
gaps.observed_evidence: The data-validation guide explicitly documents X-Goog-Hash on JSON single-request media uploads and checksum mismatch HTTP 400. Its Content-MD5 statement applies to XML single-request uploads. The linked hash reference documents base64 MD5/CRC32C, big-endian CRC32C and comma/repeated-header equivalence, but not duplicate algorithm conflict policy. The JSON header inventory omits X-Goog-Hash, and the status catalog does not specify a checksum mismatch reason.

gaps.title: Missing Content-Type acceptance for JSON media upload is not established
gaps.required_resolution: Distinguish default serving MIME type from acceptance of a missing request header. Confirm upload request behavior before claiming exact parity; if missing Content-Type is accepted locally with application/octet-stream, name that convenience as a deviation and cover it in a wire test.
gaps.observed_evidence: The JSON Content-Type reference calls the header required for object POST/PUT uploads (or supplied in metadata), and insert lists it among generally required headers. The Object resource says an object stored without Content-Type is served as application/octet-stream. The latter does not establish whether media uploads lacking the header are accepted.

gaps.title: Object response headers and opaque resource encodings need direct evidence
gaps.required_resolution: Verify the JSON download generation/metageneration/hash headers with pinned official SDK assertions or authorized differential evidence. Include partial responses: Accept-Ranges, representation metadata, full-object hashes and stored-content headers are locally asserted, but exhaustive Google 206 header presence is unverified. Track all emitted/omitted headers, including ETag and stored-content-encoding, and the rendered timeFinalized resource field. Treat exact id, ETag and generated URL encoding/spelling as opaque local choices unless exact upstream bytes are independently established. The public/private cache matrix and selected-record XML GET/HEAD metadata are locally verified in docs/en/evidence/public-object-reads.md; obtain independent service evidence before claiming complete wire parity. Establish exact XML ETag bytes, private XML default, custom-header encoding/collisions and exhaustive full/partial/HEAD header sets before claiming complete response parity. See docs/en/slices/public-object-reads.md; an SDK byte read does not prove every optional header is present.
gaps.observed_evidence: The JSON header reference documents ETag, X-Goog-Stored-Content-Encoding (identity when absent) and X-Goog-Stored-Content-Length; the XML reference additionally specifies x-goog-generation/metageneration/hash. The checked JSON sources do not enumerate an exhaustive media response set. The Object resource describes id contents, ETag meaning, links and timeFinalized but does not fix an exact id concatenation or ETag encoding. Rechecked on 2026-10-22: the public-read contract now specifies allUsers-based public classification, stored public Cache-Control or public, max-age=3600, private JSON no-cache regardless of stored metadata, and XML honoring stored directives. The private XML fallback private, max-age=0 is local, consistent with the HEAD example rather than an exhaustive default rule. The metadata guide qualifies XML ETags as MD5 for ordinary non-composite/non-XML-multipart objects using Google-managed encryption; arbitrary JSON ETag reuse must not be called exact XML parity. Exact hexadecimal/base64 representation and advanced-object ETags remain wire questions. The pinned Go XML reader parses generation, metageneration, Content-Range, Last-Modified, Cache-Control, content type/encoding, custom metadata and CRC32C; it uses stored encoding for decompression but does not parse stored-content-length. HTTP-unrepresentable JSON custom metadata and case collisions explicitly return XML 501 without changing JSON metadata. Local XML ETags are quoted lowercase hexadecimal MD5. Complete wire encoding and exhaustive header parity remain unverified under SPEC-XML-INPUTS.

gaps.title: Accepted invocation tokens do not replay responses; media and multipart uploads require generation-match
gaps.observed_evidence: Pinned Go Storage v1.70.0 attaches X-Goog-Gcs-Idempotency-Token to object operations even with RetryNever. GET/DELETE and metadata update retain local acceptance without deduplication; retries re-execute, so repeated DELETE returns 404 after its first 204. Media and multipart uploads now accept one nonempty token only with ifGenerationMatch (including zero); otherwise they return 501 before body input. Retrying a committed conditioned upload returns 412 without another generation. The pinned v1.70.0 resumable Writer also sends a token at initiation: one nonempty token is accepted without ifGenerationMatch because initiation only creates another bounded session and never mutates object state. Retried initiation returns a distinct capability, not a replayed response; stored conditions still apply atomically at finalization. Session writes accept one nonempty chunk token while offsets govern retries. Empty or duplicate tokens return 400 invalidParameter. Shared validation also applies to objects.list and PATCH, without dedicated HTTP tests for those malformed-token cases. No response replay or token-keyed deduplication exists.
gaps.required_resolution: Keep affected rows PARTIAL and record conditioned acceptance without replay. Implement and verify bounded, time-scoped response replay before claiming production retry-token fidelity; extend malformed-token HTTP coverage to listing and PATCH. Do not strip SDK headers or describe generation conditions as deduplication. See docs/en/slices/json-object-multipart.md and docs/en/evidence/multipart.md.

gaps.title: Legacy JSON metadata input handling and retry fidelity need independent evidence
gaps.observed_evidence: Legacy JSON references separate writable fields but do not establish how every changed read-only or unknown input is handled; Discovery lacks readOnly annotations. AIP-203 requires OUTPUT_ONLY values to be ignored, without establishing retroactive application to this legacy JSON API. Locally, identical server-managed values are accepted inside the update transaction; changed/unmodeled output fields, unknown fields, empty custom metadata keys and non-ASCII fixed header values return 501 notImplemented. SDK Update invocation tokens are accepted without replay, extending SPEC-013; an unconditional retry may increment metageneration again. Pinned Go sends individual empty custom values unchanged and an empty map as null, so empty string preservation and empty-map deletion are verified separately from JSON null key deletion. The general metadata guide describes stored response cache directives, while the protocol-specific JSON header reference requires no-cache for nonpublic objects; the more specific JSON rule is implemented, and the public-read contract now defines IAM allUsers classification, stored public directives and the public, max-age=3600 default. allAuthenticatedUsers alone does not classify an object as anonymously public. XML stored directives are protocol-specific; its private default is declared local. The public/private cache classification, stored directives and explicit XML metadata rejection now pass final wire/Go/guide checks in docs/en/evidence/public-object-reads.md; full provider metadata/input parity remains open. Gzip media requiring transcoding returns 501; gzip/wildcard q values or stored no-transform control unchanged-byte delivery; explicit gzip q=0 overrides wildcard and invalid/duplicate negotiation values return 400; double-compression detection is not implemented.
gaps.required_resolution: Keep affected rows PARTIAL. Verify legacy service handling of read-only/unknown inputs and scalar empty/null edge cases with an explicitly authorized differential fixture; implement bounded token response replay and streaming transcoding before claiming those semantics. Retain the final local IAM classification/cache evidence in docs/en/evidence/public-object-reads.md while obtaining independent provider evidence for the remaining metadata/input questions. Preserve explicit advanced-field rejection and the 8 KiB final custom metadata limit. See docs/en/slices/json-object-metadata.md and docs/en/evidence/object-metadata.md.

gaps.title: Multipart MIME limits, content-type precedence and checksum-container errors need direct service evidence
gaps.observed_evidence: The official upload guide defines metadata then media; data validation additionally shows a third CRC32C JSON part. References do not settle conflicting contentType precedence, exact malformed-container error reasons or emulator MIME caps. Locally, nonempty metadata contentType wins over media Content-Type then application/octet-stream; null/empty falls back. JSON parts cap at 65536 bytes, preamble/epilogue at 4096, part header blocks at 8192 including line/blank CRLF, and delimiter suffix lines at 8192 excluding CRLF. Preamble excludes the first delimiter CRLF. Known Content-Length above media cap plus 256 KiB fails early. Framing/type/header/truncation and body transport errors/trailers return 400 invalidParameter; malformed JSON returns parseError; checksum mismatch and unknown third-part keys return invalid. MD5 in the third part, an empty checksum object and equal duplicate declarations are accepted; conflicting declarations return invalidParameter. Folded/duplicate part headers, non-binary Content-Transfer-Encoding (including 7bit/8bit), and a headers-only part without the additional CRLF expected by the parser are rejected. Outer boundary and type=application/json are supported; alternate-root semantics return 501. These local rules have wire tests, not authorized real-service differential evidence or CPU/RSS measurements.
gaps.required_resolution: Keep multipart and affected method/behavior rows PARTIAL while deviations remain. Obtain an explicitly authorized direct-service fixture for MIME boundaries/caps, empty-part CRLF, transfer encodings, contentType conflicts/null/empty values, third-part MD5/unknown/conflicting fields and exact malformed/transport error reasons. Preserve bounded streaming, early metadata validation and failed-overwrite resource snapshots. See docs/en/slices/json-object-multipart.md and docs/en/evidence/multipart.md.

gaps.title: Bucket IAM normalization parity and missing-allocator startup fixture remain unverified
gaps.observed_evidence: The official policy references define bindings and bytes etags but do not establish duplicate-binding/member normalization or mixed-alphabet/non-zero-trailing-bit behavior. Locally duplicate members and repeated role bindings retain submitted order, standard/URL-safe padded/unpadded bytes compare equivalently, mixed alphabets are accepted and non-zero trailing bits return 400 invalid. Existing Rust/Go/Compose logs prove the declared local subset, not cloud normalization parity. Startup enforces the policy_revision singleton invariant but lacks a dedicated missing-row fixture; tested stale allocators and missing/orphan bucket policies do not establish that distinct fixture.

gaps.title: Strict authentication error wire details and missing-bucket authorization need real-service evidence
gaps.observed_evidence: The status-code reference (last updated 2026-10-21) documents the 401 required example with locationType header and location Authorization, the authError reason and the 403 forbidden example. It does not document the authError message or location fields, the longer principal/permission 403 message often returned by the service, or whether WWW-Authenticate is sent. Locally, invalid or unsupported credentials return 401 authError with message Invalid Credentials, locationType header and location Authorization; permission failures return the short documented Forbidden example; no WWW-Authenticate header is sent. The missing-bucket rule is local: an authenticated caller receives 404 only when it holds the required permission in at least one project, otherwise 403; the public-read contract now evaluates anonymous callers through allUsers bindings before denying them with JSON 401 required. allUsers matches anonymous and registered callers; allAuthenticatedUsers matches only registered local identities. Invalid/unregistered bearers still fail authentication and never become anonymous, even when a public grant exists. projection=full requires no extra permission because ACL/owner fields are not rendered. Authentication precedes route syntax validation, so an invalid token wins over a 400 while an anonymous malformed request still returns 400. For an objects.insert that would overwrite a live object, generation/metageneration preconditions are evaluated before the storage.objects.delete overwrite check, so a caller lacking that permission can distinguish a matching from a mismatching generation through 403 versus 412; the real-service order is unverified. Strict operations recheck the authorized bucket project inside their catalog transaction (a bucket recreated in another project returns 403 without mutation). Bucket IAM now grants permissions through the union of the selected owning project's roles and matching unconditional bucket bindings inside the operation transaction. A bucket-only caller can access a granted existing bucket but still receives 403 for a missing bucket when it lacks the permission in every project. IAM get/set use storage.buckets.getIamPolicy/setIamPolicy and retain the same anonymous, missing-bucket and local check-order rules; transaction-time authorization precedes etag comparison. Final Rust, Go and source-built strict Compose evidence is in docs/en/evidence/bucket-iam.md; it is not real-service differential evidence. The 2026-10-22 XML status reference lists 400 InvalidAuthentication for invalid or unsupported authorization headers, 401 AuthenticationRequired for missing credentials, and 403 AccessDenied, the latter independent of object existence; it does not establish the exact status/message for this local identity registry. The public-read contract locally selects anonymous 401 AuthenticationRequired, invalid-credential and strict signature-attempt 400 InvalidAuthentication and registered permission-denial 403 AccessDenied with XML Error/Code/Message. Authorized missing buckets/objects use 404 NoSuchBucket/NoSuchKey; unauthorized resources keep the denial. HEAD error bodies are explicitly absent in the official method reference. JSON credentials retain 401 required/authError. Anonymous JSON mutations and bucket/policy methods now evaluate their exact granted permissions; public object-viewer grants never imply write or policy permissions. No XML real-service request was made.
